# Reading the signal mast — field notes, part 4

*Invented material. See the README of the demo project.*

The flag code is easier to hold as a picture than as a list, so this note keeps
the sheet the harbour office hands out and says what is on it. The picture is
linked, not embedded — which is the point of this file: `/ingest` has to follow
the link relative to *this* file to find it.

![The six flags of the Kestrel code and what each one means](diagrams/signal-flags.png)

Six flags, read left to right, top row then bottom:

- **Red** — harbour closed. Nothing enters or leaves until it comes down.
- **Yellow** — quarantine aboard. The boat anchors off and waits for the office.
- **Blue** — mail boat expected within the hour.
- **Green** — free passage.
- **Black** — surge warning. Read it with the warning stages, not on its own.
- **Red barred** — answer flag: your message was received and understood.

The barred red is the one people get wrong. It is not a weaker red closure; it
is an acknowledgement, and it is the only flag that ever flies *below* another.
